answer: Each agent first solves the named cedar Sudoku puzzle with one fixed solver and commits the hash of the 9 by 9 grid plus solve time within 10 minutes. The verifier re-solves it, compares grid hashes, and checks the zenith row and timber column before acceptance. One honest agent runs 1 solve on 2 CPU cores for a 150 POA bond, while 10 fakes must run 10 solves on 20 cores, so compute cost rises 10X. A mismatched grid hash, wrong solver version, or timeout slashes the 150 POA bond and freezes repeat offenders.
